clean_text: हाँ, आपका सोचना बिल्कुल सही है! Delhi EV Policy 1.0 (जो 2020 में आई थी) में भी इलेक्ट्रिक गाड़ियों पर Road Tax और Registration Fee पूरी तरह से माफ़ (100% Exempted) थी। ​तो फिर EV Policy 2.0 (2026) में नया क्या है? सरकार ने इस बार नियमों में कुछ बड़े बदलाव किए हैं, जिन्हें आपको गाड़ी खरीदने से पहले जान लेना चाहिए: ​1. ₹30 लाख की लिमिट (नया नियम) ​पहले (Policy 1.0): आप कितनी भी महंगी इलेक्ट्रिक कार खरीदें (चाहे ₹15 लाख की हो या ₹60 लाख की), रोड टैक्स पूरी तरह माफ़ था। ​अब (Policy 2.0): रोड टैक्स और रजिस्ट्रेशन फीस की 100% छूट केवल उन्हीं इलेक्ट्रिक कारों पर मिलेगी जिनकी एक्स-शोरूम कीमत ₹30 लाख से कम है। अगर कार ₹30 लाख से ऊपर की है, तो आपको नॉर्मल टैक्स देना पड़ सकता है। ​2. डायरेक्ट परचेज सब्सिडी बंद, अब केवल स्क्रैपेज पर फोकस ​पहले (Policy 1.0): जब यह पॉलिसी शुरू हुई थी, तब नई इलेक्ट्रिक कार खरीदने पर बिना किसी पुरानी कार को बदले भी ₹1.5 लाख तक की सीधी सब्सिडी (Incentive) मिलती थी (जो बाद में कार्स के लिए बंद हो गई थी)। ​अब (Policy 2.0): अब सरकार ने साफ कर दिया है कि अगर आपको ₹1 लाख का बड़ा कैश बेनेफिट चाहिए, तो वो केवल पुरानी गाड़ी को स्क्रैप (कबाड़ में देने) पर ही मिलेगा। यानी सीधे नई गाड़ी खरीदने पर वो पुरानी सब्सिडी नहीं मिलेगी, जो आपके केस में आपकी Tiago को स्क्रैप करने पर काम आएगी।

clean_text: Great episode‼️ It is a huge misconception that hybrids don't enjoy tax sops. Under the GST 2.0 reforms, the central government completely fixed that historical anomaly that paralyzed the small car hybrid segment. In the older regime, all hybrids were taxed a blanket 43% GST (28% + 15% cess) irrespective of their size. This meant that while larger luxury hybrids enjoyed up to a 7% tax advantage, smaller mass-market hybrids had to pay an additional 12% to 14% tax compared to standard small ICE cars‼️ This absolute tax penalty is exactly why this segment was historically non-existent. With GST 2.0, sub-4m hybrids with a petrol engine under 1200cc now cleanly qualify for the entry-level 18% GST slab. Which makes the Series Hybrid architecture a brilliant candidate for urban mobility, delivering phenomenal urban fuel efficiency (25–35 km/l). But engineering can only do so much when toxic air pollution is literally choking our cities, driving up cancer rates, and scaring away long-term global investments. That is why Delhi’s new EV Policy 2.0 deserves massive credit. By setting hard registration deadlines—like transitioning all new three-wheelers by 2027 and two-wheelers by 2028 entirely to pure electric—Delhi is taking the brutal, necessary steps to force a structural shift. While the central government's tax structure gives us the perfect transition tools for passenger cars, Delhi's aggressive framework shows the kind of political will needed to clean our skies. Here’s hoping the rest of the country follows suit and aligns state-level urgency with federal tax incentives to tackle this public health crisis head-on‼️

clean_text: Let's clarify a few things here. 1. Unlike what the anchor is suggesting, the subsidy for e-2w hasn't really gone down. It had gone down last FY when FAME2 was replaced with EMPS scheme with a capped value of 10000 INR subsidy, now, it has been replaced with 5000 rs/kwh with a maximum of 10000INR subsidy per vehicle, most electric 2W already has 2 kwh or more battery capacity, so essentially the total subsidy remains the same. In the next year too, when the subsidy will further be reduced to 2500 rs/kwh at a capped value of 10000 rs/unit, even then the higher variants of Ola, Ather, TVS etc which already have approximatey 4 kwh battery packs will get the full 10000 rupess subsidy, only the lower variants with smaller pack will have reduced subsidy next year, but they are already cheaper. So, it's logical. 2. The electric cars were already not getting subsidy since FAME2 was revised, only the fleet cars were getting subsidies, now instead of focussing on fleet cars which basically serve one or two passenger, the focus is more on the buses(both intra and intercity), which will have more impact on emission as they carry much longer distance and many more passengers over their lifetime. the 2w and 3w EV industry has already matured in India and are already in a position to thrive without subsidies, the number says exactly that, everytime the subsidies went down in the recent past, the sales dropped for a while and then they rose back to the exact same level. Also, people are forgetting, instead for directly giving subsidies to the OEMs/vehicle at sales level a lot of indirect benefits are being given to the OEMs at manufacturing level in terms o PLI Scheme.
